ipc_channel_type.title: IPC Channel Type
ipc_channel_type.description: The type of IPC mechanism used for communication between processes, which affects available authentication primitives, integrity controls, and ease of exploitation.

client_authentication_enforced.title: Client Authentication Enforced on IPC Endpoint
client_authentication_enforced.description: Whether the IPC endpoint requires connecting clients to authenticate themselves to the server, enabling mutual authentication rather than one-way or no authentication.

access_restricted_to_authorized_uids_gid.title: IPC Access Restricted to Authorized UIDs/GIDs
access_restricted_to_authorized_uids_gid.description: Whether the IPC endpoint enforces filesystem permissions, D-Bus policy rules, or OS-level ACLs that restrict which UIDs or GIDs may connect, acting as a compensating control when application-level mutual authentication is absent.

sensitive_data_transmitted.title: Sensitive Data Transmitted Over IPC Channel
sensitive_data_transmitted.description: Whether the IPC channel carries credentials, tokens, PII, session identifiers, or other sensitive information that would be exposed to unauthorized processes if controls are missing.

mac_or_checksum_enforced.title: MAC or Checksum Enforced on Messages
mac_or_checksum_enforced.description: Whether the application applies a cryptographic MAC (e.g., HMAC-SHA256) or strong checksum to each message written to and verified on read from the IPC channel (shared memory segment or message queue).

segment_write_access_restricted.title: Write Access Restricted to Authorized Processes Only
segment_write_access_restricted.description: Whether OS-level permissions on the shared memory segment or message queue restrict write access exclusively to the intended producer processes, preventing arbitrary co-resident processes from writing.

replay_protection_mechanism.title: Replay Protection Mechanism
replay_protection_mechanism.description: The type of replay protection implemented in IPC message handling (sequence numbers, timestamps, nonces, multiple mechanisms, or none).

message_carries_sensitive_action.title: Messages Trigger Sensitive Actions
message_carries_sensitive_action.description: Whether IPC messages on this channel can trigger sensitive or destructive actions such as financial transactions, privilege changes, command execution, or critical state modification.

message_integrity_verification_enabled.title: Message Integrity Verification Enabled
message_integrity_verification_enabled.description: Whether IPC messages are cryptographically authenticated (e.g., via HMAC or digital signature) to detect tampering and verify authenticity before processing.

credential_verification_enforced.title: Peer Credential Verification Enforced
credential_verification_enforced.description: Whether the D-Bus service implementation checks the caller's UID/GID credentials before allowing method invocations on sensitive interfaces.

polkit_authorization_required.title: PolicyKit Authorization Required
polkit_authorization_required.description: Whether the D-Bus service requires PolicyKit (polkit) authorization for privileged method calls, as defined in its .policy file and enforced at runtime.

exposed_method_privilege_level.title: Exposed Method Privilege Level
exposed_method_privilege_level.description: The privilege level required by the operations exposed via the D-Bus interface — whether they are unprivileged, partially privileged, or fully privileged system operations.

dbus_service_bus_type.title: D-Bus Service Bus Type
dbus_service_bus_type.description: Whether the D-Bus service is registered on the system bus (accessible to all local users) or the session bus (scoped to a user session).

pipe_directory_world_writable.title: Named Pipe Directory Is World-Writable
pipe_directory_world_writable.description: Whether the directory containing the named pipe has world-writable permissions (e.g., /tmp or similar sticky-bit-absent directories), allowing any local user to pre-create the pipe name.

pipe_name_predictable.title: Named Pipe Has Predictable Name
pipe_name_predictable.description: Whether the named pipe uses a static, guessable name (e.g., /tmp/myapp.pipe) rather than a name incorporating a random or per-session token that an attacker cannot predict in advance.

pipe_ownership_verified.title: Application Verifies Pipe Ownership Before Connecting
pipe_ownership_verified.description: Whether the application checks that the named pipe it is about to connect to is owned by the expected user/process before establishing the connection, preventing connection to an attacker-pre-created pipe.

ipc_rate_limiting_enabled.title: IPC Rate Limiting Enabled
ipc_rate_limiting_enabled.description: Whether ingress rate limiting or connection throttling is configured on the IPC channel (Unix domain socket, named pipe, loopback TCP, or message queue endpoint).

socket_buffer_limit_configured.title: Socket Buffer Limit Configured
socket_buffer_limit_configured.description: Whether explicit socket buffer or message queue depth limits are configured to prevent resource exhaustion under flooding conditions.

loopback_rpc_tls_enabled.title: Loopback RPC TLS Enabled
loopback_rpc_tls_enabled.description: Whether TLS is enabled on the loopback RPC/gRPC/REST endpoint (e.g., grpc.WithTransportCredentials vs grpc.WithInsecure, or https vs http scheme for loopback-bound listeners).

certificate_validation_mode.title: Certificate Validation Mode
certificate_validation_mode.description: How the RPC client validates the server certificate when TLS is enabled: 'full' (system CA or pinned cert), 'skip_verify' (InsecureSkipVerify=true), or 'self_signed_no_pin' (accepts self-signed certs without certificate pinning).

ipc_header_field_encryption_enabled.title: IPC Header/Metadata Field-Level Encryption Enabled
ipc_header_field_encryption_enabled.description: Whether application-level field encryption is applied to sensitive fields (credentials, tokens, PII) within IPC message headers, D-Bus signal payloads, or RPC metadata before transmission over the channel.

sensitive_field_types_in_headers.title: Sensitive Field Types Present in IPC Headers or Metadata
sensitive_field_types_in_headers.description: List of sensitive data categories found in IPC message headers, D-Bus signal metadata, or RPC call metadata (e.g., 'credentials', 'auth_token', 'session_id', 'pii', 'api_key').

channel_access_restricted_to_intended_pr.title: IPC Channel Access Restricted to Intended Processes
channel_access_restricted_to_intended_pr.description: Whether the IPC channel enforces access controls (e.g., filesystem permissions on socket/pipe, D-Bus policy rules, SELinux/AppArmor labels) that prevent unintended co-resident processes from observing message headers or metadata.
